2.headline: AI Company Anthropic Sets a Stock Market Record
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Can one company be worth over one trillion dollars on its first day? Anthropic just did it.

Anthropic is an AI company. It makes the AI helper called Claude. On Thursday, it began selling its shares on the stock market in New York. A share is a small piece of a company. Now ordinary people can buy them.

The price for one share was 83 dollars. But the first sale was at 111 dollars and 50 cents. That is a rise of more than 30 percent. The company raised about 80 billion dollars. News reports say this is the biggest amount ever. It beat the space company SpaceX.
Anthropic started in 2021. Its main rival is OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT.
Why is this important? Many people use AI tools every day. This sale shows that investors believe in AI. But some experts are worried. They think AI prices may be too high and could fall later.
To sum up, Anthropic sold its shares to the public, and it set a new record.
Thank you for listening.

3.headline: Anthropic's Stock Market Debut Breaks a Record
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
What happens when an AI company sells its shares to the public for the first time? On Thursday, the answer was a new record.

According to news reports, Anthropic, the company that makes the AI assistant Claude, started trading on the Nasdaq stock market in New York on Thursday. This was its IPO, or initial public offering. An IPO means a private company sells its shares to ordinary investors for the first time.

Each share was priced at 83 dollars. But the first trade was at 111 dollars and 50 cents, a jump of more than 30 percent. The company raised about 80 billion dollars. Reports say that is the most money ever raised in a stock offering. It beat the rocket company SpaceX, which went public in June.
At the IPO price, Anthropic was valued at about 1.5 trillion dollars. Demand for the shares was very strong.
Anthropic was started in 2021 by former leaders at OpenAI, which is now its main rival. OpenAI has delayed its own IPO until next year.

Why does this matter? Many people around the world use AI tools every day, and now ordinary investors can own a piece of one of the biggest AI makers. But there are also worries. Some experts fear an AI bubble. A bubble means prices rise much higher than the real value, and then they can fall quickly. Reports also say the company is not yet making a profit.
To sum up, Anthropic's first day on the stock market set a new record, and its share price jumped by more than 30 percent.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
AI 회사가 처음으로 일반인에게 주식을 팔면 어떤 일이 생길까요? 목요일, 그 답은 새로운 기록이었습니다.
언론 보도에 따르면, AI 비서 클로드를 만드는 회사 앤트로픽이 목요일 뉴욕의 나스닥 주식 시장에서 거래를 시작했습니다. 이것이 이 회사의 IPO, 즉 기업공개였습니다. IPO란 비상장 회사가 처음으로 일반 투자자들에게 주식을 파는 것을 뜻합니다.
주식 한 주의 가격은 83달러로 정해졌습니다. 하지만 첫 거래는 111달러 50센트에 이루어져 30퍼센트 넘게 뛰었습니다. 회사는 약 800억 달러를 모았습니다. 보도에 따르면 이는 주식 공모로 모은 돈 가운데 역대 최대입니다. 지난 6월 상장한 로켓 회사 스페이스X를 넘어섰습니다.
공모가 기준으로 앤트로픽의 가치는 약 1조 5천억 달러로 평가되었습니다. 주식에 대한 수요는 매우 강했습니다.

4.headline: Anthropic Raises About $80 Billion in Record IPO
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Wall Street has just seen its biggest stock market debut ever, and it came from the world of artificial intelligence.

According to the Associated Press, Anthropic, the San Francisco-based developer of the Claude AI assistant, began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT. The company priced its initial public offering at 83 dollars a share, above its earlier target range of 70 to 78 dollars.

When trading opened just before noon, the first shares changed hands at 111 dollars and 50 cents, more than 30 percent above the offer price. The stock later eased back to around 100 dollars, according to reports.

Anthropic raised roughly 80 billion dollars, which reports describe as the largest amount ever raised in an IPO, topping the roughly 75 billion dollars raised by SpaceX in June. At the offer price, the company was valued at about 1.5 trillion dollars.
Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI leaders, Anthropic competes with OpenAI, Google and a number of American and Chinese startups. OpenAI has postponed its own market listing until next year.

The debut matters well beyond the United States. Investors around the world are watching whether the enormous sums being poured into AI will pay off. Analysts pointed to strong demand for the shares as a sign of confidence in the industry, and chief executive Dario Amodei has said the company aims to keep humans in control of AI. However, the company is still unprofitable, carries billions of dollars in debt, and has committed to spending heavily on computing power. Some observers also warn that AI stocks could be forming a bubble.
To sum up, Anthropic's record-breaking IPO raised about 80 billion dollars, and its shares jumped by more than 30 percent in their first trade.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.

정오 직전 거래가 시작되자 첫 주식은 공모가보다 30퍼센트 넘게 높은 111달러 50센트에 거래되었습니다. 보도에 따르면 주가는 이후 100달러 안팎으로 다소 내려왔습니다.
앤트로픽은 약 800억 달러를 조달했으며, 보도들은 이를 IPO 사상 최대 조달액이라고 전합니다. 이는 스페이스X가 6월에 조달한 약 750억 달러를 넘어선 것입니다. 공모가 기준으로 회사 가치는 약 1조 5천억 달러로 평가되었습니다.
2021년 오픈AI 출신 간부들이 세운 앤트로픽은 오픈AI, 구글, 그리고 여러 미국과 중국 스타트업과 경쟁하고 있습니다. 오픈AI는 자체 상장을 내년으로 미뤘습니다.

이번 데뷔는 미국을 훨씬 넘어서는 의미가 있습니다. 전 세계 투자자들은 AI에 쏟아붓는 막대한 돈이 성과를 낼지 지켜보고 있습니다. 분석가들은 주식에 대한 강한 수요를 업계에 대한 신뢰의 표시로 꼽았고, 다리오 아모데이 최고경영자는 회사가 인간이 AI를 계속 통제하도록 하는 것을 목표로 한다고 말해 왔습니다. 하지만 회사는 아직 적자이고, 수십억 달러의 부채를 안고 있으며, 컴퓨팅 능력에 막대한 돈을 쓰기로 약속했습니다. 일부 관찰자들은 AI 주식에 거품이 생기고 있을 수 있다고 경고합니다.
정리하면, 앤트로픽의 기록적인 IPO는 약 800억 달러를 조달했고, 주가는 첫 거래에서 30퍼센트 넘게 뛰었습니다.

5.headline: Anthropic Shatters IPO Fundraising Record as Shares Soar
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
In a debut that shattered fundraising records, Anthropic has become a publicly traded company, and investors could hardly get enough of it.

The San Francisco-based maker of the Claude chatbot began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT, according to the Associated Press and other outlets. The company had priced its initial public offering at 83 dollars a share, comfortably above a marketed range of 70 to 78 dollars, a telltale sign of robust appetite among institutional buyers.

That appetite spilled over once trading got under way. The first shares changed hands at 111 dollars and 50 cents, a premium of more than 30 percent, before the stock surrendered some of those gains and drifted back toward 100 dollars by midday.

All told, the offering raised roughly 80 billion dollars, eclipsing the approximately 75 billion dollars SpaceX raised in its own blockbuster listing in June and making it, by that measure, the largest IPO on record. At the offer price, Anthropic commanded a valuation of around 1.5 trillion dollars.

Founded in 2021 by a group of former OpenAI executives, Anthropic is locked in a fierce race for dominance with OpenAI, Google and a crop of American and Chinese challengers. OpenAI, for its part, has pushed back its own flotation until next year.

The stakes extend far beyond Wall Street. Investors worldwide have a vested interest in whether the staggering sums being funneled into artificial intelligence will ultimately deliver returns. Bullish analysts hailed the pricing as a vote of confidence in the sector, and chief executive Dario Amodei has said the company's goal is to keep humans firmly in control of the technology.

Yet the euphoria comes with caveats. The company remains unprofitable by standard accounting measures, shoulders several billion dollars in debt, and has signed up for vast commitments on computing infrastructure. Skeptics warn that AI valuations may be inflating into a bubble, and that a correction, if it comes, could be painful.

To sum up, Anthropic's market debut raised a record sum of about 80 billion dollars, and its shares leapt more than 30 percent at the open, a striking measure of investor faith in AI, tempered by lingering doubts.
Thank you for listening.

1.headline: A Van Gogh Painting Sells for a Record Price
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
A painting sold for a very big price.
The painting is by Vincent van Gogh. He was a famous artist. He painted it in France in 1890. It shows tall trees with pink flowers. The trees are chestnut trees.

On Wednesday, it sold in New York. The sale was at an auction. At an auction, people offer money, and the highest offer wins. The price was about one hundred ninety million dollars. This is a new record for van Gogh.
Did you know? Van Gogh sold very few paintings in his life. Now his paintings cost a lot of money.
Again, a van Gogh painting sold for a record price.
Thank you for listening.

2.headline: Van Gogh Painting Sells for a Record $190 Million
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Would you pay 190 million dollars for one painting? Someone in New York just did.
On Wednesday, a painting by Vincent van Gogh sold at an auction in New York. At an auction, people offer prices, and the highest offer wins. The final price was 190.4 million dollars, including fees.
The painting is called Blossoming Chestnut Trees. It shows tall trees with pink flowers over a sunny street. Van Gogh painted it in a small town in France in 1890. He died about two months later.
This is a new record for a van Gogh painting. The old record was 117.2 million dollars in 2022. The buyer was an art dealer from New York.
The painting also has a sad past. A Jewish family in Germany sold it in 1936, under pressure from the Nazis. Just before the sale, the family's heirs and the owners made an agreement.
Did you know? Van Gogh sold very few paintings while he was alive.

3.headline: Van Gogh's Blossoming Trees Sell for a Record $190.4 Million
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
How much would you pay for a painting of trees in bloom? One buyer in New York just paid 190.4 million dollars.

According to news reports, a painting by the Dutch artist Vincent van Gogh sold for a record 190.4 million dollars, including fees, at Sotheby's auction house in New York on Wednesday. An auction is a sale where people compete by offering higher and higher prices.

The painting is called Blossoming Chestnut Trees. It shows tall chestnut trees covered in pink flowers above a sunny street. Van Gogh painted it in May 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise, a small town in France. He died there about two months later.

The price is a new record for a van Gogh painting at auction. The old record was 117.2 million dollars, set in 2022 by a painting called Orchard with Cypresses. The buyer this time was William Acquavella, a well-known art dealer in New York.

The painting also has a long history. In 1909, a Jewish publisher in Berlin named Samuel Fischer bought it. His family sold it in 1936, when Nazi pressure on Jewish families was growing in Germany. His heirs, or family members who receive property after someone dies, asked for the sale to be delayed. One day before the auction, Sotheby's said the heirs and the current owners had reached an agreement.
Did you know? Van Gogh sold very few paintings during his lifetime. Today, his works are some of the most valuable in the world.
To sum up, a van Gogh painting of blooming chestnut trees sold for a record 190.4 million dollars in New York.
Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Van Gogh Painting Fetches Record $190.4 Million at Sotheby's
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
A painting that Vincent van Gogh finished only weeks before his death has become the most expensive work by the artist ever sold at auction.

According to the Associated Press, Blossoming Chestnut Trees fetched 190.4 million dollars, including fees, at Sotheby's in New York on Wednesday. The buyer was William Acquavella, head of the Manhattan gallery Acquavella Galleries.

The canvas depicts towering chestnut trees heavy with pink blossoms above a sunlit street. Van Gogh painted it in May 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise, a village north of Paris, shortly after leaving a psychiatric hospital. He died there that July.
The sale easily surpassed the previous auction record for the artist, 117.2 million dollars, paid in 2022 for Orchard with Cypresses.

The painting also carries a complicated history. It was bought in Paris in 1909 by Samuel Fischer, a Jewish publisher based in Berlin. His family sold it in 1936 as Nazi persecution intensified in Germany. A lawyer for Fischer's heirs argued that the sale took place under pressure and asked Sotheby's to postpone the auction. On Tuesday, however, the auction house announced that the heirs and the current owners, an Argentine family who acquired the work in 1975, had reached a settlement. The terms were not disclosed.
The result shows that the very best works of art can still attract enormous sums from collectors. It also shows how questions about ownership during the Nazi era continue to shape major sales today.
Did you know? Van Gogh sold very few paintings during his lifetime and struggled financially for most of his career.
To sum up, a van Gogh landscape sold for a record 190.4 million dollars in New York, after a last-minute agreement with the heirs of its former Jewish owner.
Thank you for listening.

이 그림에는 복잡한 역사도 있습니다. 1909년 베를린의 유대인 출판업자 자무엘 피셔가 파리에서 이 그림을 샀습니다. 그의 가족은 독일에서 나치의 박해가 심해지던 1936년 그림을 팔았습니다. 피셔 상속인들의 변호사는 그 판매가 압박 속에서 이루어졌다고 주장하며 소더비에 경매 연기를 요청했습니다. 그러나 화요일, 경매 회사는 상속인들과 1975년 이 작품을 사들인 아르헨티나 가족인 현 소유자들이 합의에 이르렀다고 발표했습니다. 합의 조건은 공개되지 않았습니다.

5.headline: Late Van Gogh Landscape Smashes Auction Record at $190.4 Million
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Blossoms painted in the final months of Vincent van Gogh's life have set the art world abuzz, and smashed a record in the process.

According to the Associated Press, Blossoming Chestnut Trees sold for 190.4 million dollars, fees included, at Sotheby's in New York on Wednesday. The winning bidder was William Acquavella, the veteran dealer who heads Acquavella Galleries on Manhattan's Upper East Side.

The work portrays a row of lofty chestnut trees laden with pink blossoms, towering over a sun-drenched street. Van Gogh completed it in May 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise, a village north of Paris where he had settled only days after his release from a psychiatric hospital. He would die there barely two months later, at the age of 37.

The price comfortably eclipsed the artist's previous auction high of 117.2 million dollars, achieved in 2022 by Orchard with Cypresses, and underscores the enduring appetite for blue-chip masterpieces at the very top of the market.

Yet the sale nearly ran aground. The painting was purchased in Paris in 1909 by Samuel Fischer, a prominent Jewish publisher in Berlin, and his family parted with it in 1936 as Nazi persecution tightened its grip on Germany. An attorney representing Fischer's heirs contended that the sale had been made under duress and urged Sotheby's to postpone the auction. Then, on Tuesday, just a day before the hammer fell, the auction house announced that the heirs and the current owners, an Argentine family that acquired the canvas in 1975, had struck an agreement. Its terms were not made public.

The episode is a reminder that, some ninety years on, questions of wartime provenance, or the documented ownership history of an artwork, continue to cast a long shadow over the trade in masterpieces.
Did you know? Van Gogh sold only a handful of paintings in his lifetime and relied heavily on his brother Theo for financial support.
To sum up, a late van Gogh landscape fetched a record 190.4 million dollars in New York, after a last-minute settlement with the heirs of its former Jewish owner cleared the way for the sale.
Thank you for listening.

p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
On Thursday, many phones in Korea made a loud sound.
Thursday was a big test day in Korea. Many students took a test for university. In the morning, the government sent an alarm to every phone. The phones were loud, even on silent.
Why? The government wanted to stop cheating. Some students may hide a phone in the test room. If the phone makes a noise, people can find it.
That morning, the government found 22 phones at test sites. Most people stayed calm about the noise.
Again, phones in Korea made loud alarms to stop cheating on the big test.

2.headline: Loud Phone Alerts Sound Across Korea on Exam Day
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
What if your phone screamed loudly, even on silent mode? That happened all over South Korea on Thursday.

Thursday was the day of the Suneung, Korea's big university entrance test. At 8:30 in the morning, the government sent an emergency alert to phones across the country. The alarm was very loud and lasted about 10 seconds.

Why did the government do this? It wanted to stop cheating. Some students might hide a phone and use AI to get answers. This kind of alert sounds even on silent mode. So a hidden phone would make a loud noise.
In the afternoon, two more surprise alerts were sent. This was the first time the government used this kind of alert against cheating.
More than 550,000 students took the test. By late morning, officials found 22 phones that students did not hand in.
Most people stayed calm. Many said it was fine for just one day.
To sum up, phones across Korea sounded loud alarms on test day to catch hidden phones and stop cheating.
Thank you for listening.

오후에는 예고 없는 경보가 두 번 더 보내졌습니다. 정부가 부정행위를 막는 데 이런 종류의 경보를 쓴 것은 이번이 처음이었습니다.
55만 명이 넘는 학생들이 시험을 봤습니다. 오전 늦게까지 당국은 학생들이 제출하지 않은 휴대폰 22대를 찾았습니다.
대부분의 사람들은 차분했습니다. 많은 사람들이 단 하루라면 괜찮다고 말했습니다.
정리하면, 숨겨진 휴대폰을 찾아 부정행위를 막기 위해 시험 날 한국 전역의 휴대폰에서 큰 경보가 울렸습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: Korea Uses Emergency Phone Alerts to Fight Exam Cheating
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Imagine your phone suddenly making a loud siren sound, even though it was set to silent. That happened across South Korea on Thursday morning.

According to news reports, at 8:30 a.m. on Thursday, the government sent a nationwide emergency alert to mobile phones. It was a test alert, and it sounded for about 10 seconds at full volume. The message asked people to cooperate because the college entrance exam, called the Suneung, was about to begin.

Why send an alarm on exam day? The goal was to catch cheating. Officials worried that some students might hide phones and use AI tools to cheat. The highest-level alert sounds even when a phone is on silent mode. So any hidden phone that was turned on would make a loud noise in the exam room.

Two more surprise alerts were sent in the afternoon. They targeted phones that had been turned off in the morning and then turned back on later. It was the first time the government used its top-level alert system to stop cheating.
More than 550,000 students took the test this year. By late morning, the Education Ministry said it had found 22 phones that students had not handed in.

Why does this matter? In Korea, the Suneung is extremely important, because it strongly affects which university students can enter. Fairness is a very big issue. According to one Korean newspaper, most people on their way to work stayed calm and said they could accept the noise for one day.
To sum up, phones across Korea sounded emergency alarms on exam day to stop students from cheating with hidden phones.
Thank you for listening.

언론 보도에 따르면, 목요일 오전 8시 30분 정부는 휴대폰으로 전국에 긴급 경보를 보냈습니다. 이것은 시험용 경보였고, 최대 음량으로 약 10초 동안 울렸습니다. 메시지는 수능이라고 불리는 대학 입학시험이 곧 시작되니 협조해 달라고 요청했습니다.
왜 시험 날에 경보를 보냈을까요? 목표는 부정행위를 잡아내는 것이었습니다. 당국은 일부 학생들이 휴대폰을 숨겨 AI 도구로 부정행위를 할까 걱정했습니다. 최고 단계의 경보는 휴대폰이 무음 모드일 때도 울립니다. 그래서 켜져 있는 숨겨진 휴대폰은 시험실에서 큰 소리를 내게 됩니다.
오후에는 예고 없는 경보가 두 번 더 보내졌습니다. 이 경보는 오전에 꺼져 있다가 나중에 다시 켜진 휴대폰을 겨냥했습니다. 정부가 부정행위를 막으려고 최고 단계의 경보 시스템을 쓴 것은 이번이 처음이었습니다.
올해 55만 명이 넘는 학생들이 시험을 봤습니다. 오전 늦게 교육부는 학생들이 제출하지 않은 휴대폰 22대를 찾았다고 밝혔습니다.
왜 이것이 중요할까요? 한국에서 수능은 학생들이 어느 대학에 들어갈 수 있는지에 큰 영향을 주기 때문에 매우 중요합니다. 공정성은 아주 큰 문제입니다. 한 한국 신문에 따르면, 출근길의 사람들 대부분은 차분했고 하루쯤은 그 소리를 참을 수 있다고 말했습니다.
정리하면, 학생들이 숨긴 휴대폰으로 부정행위를 하지 못하도록 시험 날 한국 전역의 휴대폰에서 긴급 경보가 울렸습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: South Korea Sounds Nationwide Alerts to Catch Exam Cheats
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
For about ten seconds on Thursday morning, nearly every mobile phone in South Korea let out a piercing siren, and it was all about a single exam.

According to the Korea Herald, the government sent a nationwide test alert at 8:30 a.m. through its highest-level disaster warning system, shortly before the start of the College Scholastic Ability Test, known as the Suneung. The alert ran for ten and a half seconds at maximum volume and asked the public for their cooperation.

The aim was to expose phones that test takers might have hidden in exam rooms. Top-level alerts override silent mode and reach any phone that is switched on and connected to a cellular network, so a concealed device would immediately give itself away. Two unannounced follow-up alerts went out in the afternoon to catch phones that had been switched off earlier and turned back on.

Officials tightened security after a top scorer on a separate national exam reportedly admitted to cheating with a tiny camera and generative AI. It was the first time the top-tier alert system had been used to deter cheating.

More than 550,000 students sat the test. By 11:30 a.m., the Education Ministry said it had found 22 smartphones that had not been handed in, across nine cities and provinces. However, experts noted that some modified phones can block the alerts, so the method is not foolproof.

The Suneung largely determines university admissions, so fairness is taken extremely seriously. A local newspaper reported that commuters were largely calm, with many saying they could tolerate the disruption for one day.
To sum up, South Korea used its most powerful emergency alert system on exam day to uncover hidden phones and discourage AI-assisted cheating.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Sirens on Silent: Korea Turns Disaster Alerts Against Exam Cheats
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

At 8:30 on Thursday morning, a shrill siren erupted from phones the length and breadth of South Korea, silent mode notwithstanding, and the cause was not an earthquake or an air raid, but a university entrance exam.

According to the Korea Herald, the government harnessed its highest-level disaster alert system to broadcast a nationwide test message shortly before the College Scholastic Ability Test, or Suneung, got under way. The alarm blared at maximum volume for ten and a half seconds and appealed to the public for cooperation.

The rationale was simple: to smoke out contraband phones. Top-tier cell broadcasts override silent settings and reach any handset that is powered on and connected to a mobile network, even with data switched off, meaning a phone squirreled away in an exam room would instantly betray its owner. Two unannounced follow-up alerts were dispatched in the afternoon, aimed at devices that had been turned off during the morning sweep and later switched back on.

The crackdown follows a cheating scandal on a separate national exam, in which a top scorer reportedly confessed to using a miniature camera and generative AI. Thursday marked the first time the top-level alert system had been deployed as an anti-cheating tool.
More than 550,000 students sat the exam. By late morning, the Education Ministry reported that 22 smartphones that had not been surrendered had turned up in nine cities and provinces.

The measure is not watertight, however. Reports indicate that some modified phones can suppress the alerts, a vulnerability the Interior Ministry has acknowledged, underscoring that no technological fix is entirely foolproof.

In a country where the Suneung can make or break a young person's prospects, fairness is sacrosanct. Indeed, one local daily reported that commuters took the din largely in stride, with many shrugging that they could put up with it for a single day.

To sum up, South Korea turned its most powerful emergency alert system into an exam invigilator, sounding sirens nationwide on one of the most important days of the school year to flush out hidden phones and deter AI-assisted cheating.
Thank you for listening.
